info.title: Sightline API
info.description: Every route Sightline serves. Response shapes are the ones its contract test enforces; a route that test leaves out says why. Requests are authenticated by session cookie or, in hosted mode, an API token (`Authorization: Bearer`). Generated from apps/api/src/http/contract.ts.

get.description: Response shape not covered by the contract test: A 302 to the provider's consent screen. There is no body to have a shape, and the query string it builds is asserted directly in auth/providers.test.ts.

Response shape not covered by the contract test: A 302 either into the app or back to it with a reason. Every branch is a redirect, and the claim checks behind it are asserted in auth/providers.test.ts without a network.

post.description: Response shape not covered by the contract test: 204 and a cleared cookie: no body to declare. Revocation is asserted against real rows in auth/signin.test.ts.

get.description: Response shape not covered by the contract test: Session management has no meaning in a self-hosted deployment, which has no sessions, and this suite runs self-hosted. Covered by auth/signin.test.ts.

delete.description: Response shape not covered by the contract test: Revokes one session, scoped to its owner. Covered by auth/signin.test.ts.

post.description: Response shape not covered by the contract test: Revokes every session for the caller. Covered by auth/signin.test.ts, which asserts each token is dead afterwards.

Response shape not covered by the contract test: Creates a connection and returns an ExternalId that is shown once. Calling it here would leave rows behind and put a one-time secret in a test log; the behaviour is covered by the tenancy suites.

delete.description: Response shape not covered by the contract test: Forgets a connection and purges its graph scopes. Destructive by design, so it is exercised where the rows are disposable rather than against the running app.

get.description: Response shape not covered by the contract test: Returns a one-click link carrying the connection's ExternalId. Needs a real connection to exist and would put that secret in a test log; the link's shape is asserted in packages/shared's onboarding tests, which need no database.

post.description: Response shape not covered by the contract test: Writes a role ARN derived from an account id. Mutating, and the derivation is asserted in packages/shared's onboarding tests.

Response shape not covered by the contract test: Attempts a real sts:AssumeRole into a customer account. Read-only, but it is still an outbound call per invocation, and the diagnosis it returns is asserted in connection/credentialDiagnosis.test.ts against the error shapes AWS produces.

delete.description: Response shape not covered by the contract test: Deletes the account and everything in it. Not exercised here for the obvious reason - this suite runs against a populated database and the refusal path it *can* reach (self-hosted has no account to delete) is the uninteresting half. The purge itself is asserted in tenancy/purge.test.ts, which seeds two tenants, deletes one, and checks both that nothing of it remains and that the other is untouched.

post.description: Response shape not covered by the contract test: Queues a real scan, then streams it. There is no input that makes it decline - its 409 needs a scan already queued, and reaching that state means having queued one - so calling it would scan whichever AWS account the deployment is pointed at and overwrite the graph. The events are covered by jobs/progress.test.ts, which seeds the rows they are derived from, and typed as `ScanEvent` in @sightline/shared, so a port that changes them fails typecheck. The queue itself is jobs/queue.test.ts.

get.description: Response shape not covered by the contract test: An event stream, so it has no single response body to declare, and it stays open until the scan ends. What it emits is asserted directly in jobs/progress.test.ts by seeding the rows the events are derived from - which is possible precisely because the stream is now a function of the database rather than of a live scan.

post.description: Response shape not covered by the contract test: Hosted only: this suite runs self-hosted, where every team route refuses. The rules - invites used once, roles within what the actor may grant, an owner always kept - are auth/team.test.ts against Postgres, and who may call each is auth/enforcement.test.ts.
